'''Gerald Lawrence Schroeder''' ({{Langx|he|ג'רלד לורנס שרדר}}; born 20 February 1938) is an American-Israeli [[Orthodox Judaism|Orthodox Jewish]] physicist, author, lecturer, and teacher at College of Jewish Studies [[Aish HaTorah]]'s Discovery Seminar, Essentials and Fellowships programs and Executive Learning Center,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://israel.aish.com/elc/faculty.asp |title=Executive Learning Center Faculty|access-date=2010-12-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110707101104/http://israel.aish.com/elc/faculty.asp |archive-date=7 July 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref> who focuses on what he perceives to be an inherent relationship between [[science and spirituality]].

==Education==
Schroeder received his BSc in 1959, his MSc in 1961, and his PhD in nuclear physics and earth and planetary sciences in 1965, from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://alum.mit.edu/news/AlumniProfiles/Archive/Gerald_Schroeder_-2759-2C_SM_-2761-2C_PhD_-2765 |title=Nuclear Scientist Sees No God–Science Conflict |last=Lowe |first=Chelsea |date=Sep–Oct 2006 |work=Technology Review |access-date=18 December 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110607203042/https://alum.mit.edu/news/AlumniProfiles/Archive/Gerald_Schroeder_-2759-2C_SM_-2761-2C_PhD_-2765 |archive-date=7 June 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He worked seven years on the staff of the MIT physics department. He was a member of the [[United States Atomic Energy Commission]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sullivan-county.com/x/science.htm |title=Where the Bible meets the Big Bang
|last=Sacks |first=Brian |date=2 October 2007 |access-date=18 December 2010 |publisher=sullivan-county.com}}</ref>

==Aliyah to Israel==
After [[Aliyah|immigrating]] to Israel in 1971, Schroeder was employed as a researcher at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], the [[Volcani Institute of Agricultural Research|Volcani Research Institute]], and the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].<ref>{{cite journal |url=http://www.ou.org/pdf/ja/5767/fall67/17-22.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060912232711/http://www.ou.org/pdf/ja/5767/fall67/17-22.pdf |archive-date=2006-09-12 |url-status=live |title=Finding the Intelligence Within the Design |last=Schroeder |first=Gerald |journal=Jewish Action |date=Fall 2006 |pages=17–22}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://alum.mit.edu/ne/noteworthy/profiles/schroeder.html |title=Gerald Schroeder '59 |access-date=2008-05-01 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080114081240/http://alum.mit.edu/ne/noteworthy/profiles/schroeder.html |archive-date=14 January 2008}}</ref> He currently teaches at [[Aish HaTorah|Aish HaTorah College of Jewish Studies]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.geraldschroeder.com/About.aspx |title=About Dr. Gerald Schroeder |publisher=geraldschroeder.com |access-date=18 December 2010}}</ref>

== Religion and science ==
Schroeder's works frequently cite [[Talmud]]ic, [[Midrash]]ic and medieval commentaries on the [[Genesis creation narrative|biblical creation account]], such as commentaries written by the Jewish philosopher [[Nachmanides]] while also referencing scientific discoveries. [[Antony Flew]], an academic philosopher who promoted atheism for most of his adult life, indicated that the arguments of Gerald Schroeder had influenced his late-in-life decision to become a [[deist]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.latimes.com/news/obituaries/la-me-antony-flew15-2010apr15,0,4059881.story |title=Antony Flew dies at 87; atheist philosopher who changed his mind late in life |agency=Associated Press |date=14 April 2010 |access-date=18 December 2010 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/11/04/magazine/04Flew-t.html?_r=2&pagewanted=all |title=The Turning of an Atheist |last=Oppenheimer |first=Mark |date=4 November 2007 |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=18 December 2010}}</ref>

Schroeder's ideas to reconcile faith and science have drawn some criticism from both Christians<ref>[https://answersingenesis.org/creationism/old-earth/gerald-schroeders-new-variation-on-the-day-age-theory-1/ "Gerald Schroeder and his New Variation on the 'Day-Age' Theory"], 1 August 2000</ref> and non-religious scientists.<ref>Perakh, Mark. [http://www.talkreason.org/articles/schroeder.cfm "Not a Very Big Bang About Genesis"], December 2001.</ref>  [[Natan Slifkin]] argues that Schroeder's calculations do not fit the order of creation as presented in Genesis vs. the order of organism development as dictated by our current understanding of [[evolutionary biology]].<ref>''The Challenge of Creation: Judaism's Encounter with Science, Cosmology and Evolution'' (Zoo Torah/Yashar Books 2006) ISBN 1-933143-15-0</ref>

==Personal==
Schroeder's wife Barbara Sofer is a columnist for the English-language Israeli newspaper ''[[The Jerusalem Post]]''. The couple have five children.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.jpost.com/author/barbara-sofer |title=Barbara Sofer |website=The Jerusalem Post}}</ref>

==Prizes==
In 2012, Schroeder was awarded the [[Trotter Prize (Texas A&M)|Trotter Prize]] by [[Texas A&M University]]'s College of Science.<ref>[http://www.science.tamu.edu/trotter/ Trotter Prize & Endowed Lecture Series]</ref>

==Works==
* ''Genesis and the Big Bang'' (1990), {{ISBN|0-553-35413-2}}
* ''The Science of God: The Convergence of Scientific and Biblical Wisdom'', (1997), {{ISBN|0-7679-0303-X}}
* ''The Hidden Face of God: Science Reveals the Ultimate Truth'', (2002), {{ISBN|0-7432-0325-9}}.
* ''God According to God: A Physicist Proves We've Been Wrong About God All Along'', (2009), {{ISBN|978-0-06-171015-5}}.
